headline: Caps' Vincent Desharnais out 4-6 weeks after appendectomy
take:
Vincent Desharnais is out four to six weeks after an emergency appendectomy on Thursday, the Capitals announced, per ESPN and Daily Faceoff.

The numbers say Washington loses a steadier piece than his three assists suggest. So far this season, the Capitals have controlled 54.6 percent of the expected goals (the quality of chances created and allowed) at five-on-five while Desharnais is on the ice, and the team's share runs about six percentage points better with him than without him. He has played 19.41 minutes a game, a real workload for a defenseman with no goals. That fits a role built on suppressing chances rather than producing them, so don't expect his absence to dent the scoring much, but it can show up in the defensive end. Washington already sits at 48.2 percent of expected goals overall and is 5-4-0, propped up by goaltending that has saved 4.9 goals more than expected. A thinner blue line with that cushion is worth watching. The sample is only nine games, so treat the on-ice splits as early reads, not fixed levels.
